program: NIH Exploratory/Developmental Research Project Grant (Parent R21 Clinical Trial Not Allowed), PA-25-304
direction: Biomedical informatics: machine learning on multimodal clinical data for neurodegenerative disease
title: Graph-based multimodal learning for early prediction of motor progression in Parkinson's disease
background: Parkinson's disease progresses at very different rates across patients, and this heterogeneity is a major reason disease-modifying trials fail: trials enrol patients whose symptoms will barely change within the trial window. Large open cohorts now pair longitudinal clinical ratings with structural and diffusion MRI, dopamine transporter imaging and biofluid markers, but most predictive models either use a single modality or concatenate hand-picked features, ignoring the network organisation of the brain and the missingness patterns typical of real cohorts. This exploratory project will test whether representing each patient's brain as a graph of regions, and learning jointly over imaging-derived graphs and clinical covariates with explicit handling of missing modalities, predicts two-year motor progression better than established clinical and imaging baselines. As an R21, the project is scoped to establish feasibility and effect size on existing de-identified cohort data, and to produce the validated model and analysis code needed to justify a larger prospective study.
challenges: Heterogeneous and incomplete modalities: not every participant has every scan or visit, and missingness is not random
Small effective sample size relative to model capacity, creating a high risk of overfitting and optimistic evaluation
Site and scanner effects that can masquerade as biological signal
Establishing a clinically meaningful comparison against strong, simple baselines rather than weak strawmen
Interpretability sufficient for clinicians to judge whether the learned signal is biologically plausible

budget.note: The combined budget for direct costs for the two-year project period may not exceed $275,000; no more than $200,000 may be requested in any single year.

eligibility: Standard NIH eligibility for PA-25-304 (see the NOFO); investigator and environment are scored under Factor 3, which is outside the scope of this document.
requirements: Scope the work as exploratory/developmental research at an early and conceptual stage, not a full-scale study
Preliminary data are not required but may be included
Address the scored review factors: Factor 1 Importance of the Research (Significance and Innovation) and Factor 2 Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
Propose no clinical trial (this NOFO is Clinical Trial Not Allowed); use existing de-identified data
constraints: Total project period may not exceed 2 years
Combined direct costs may not exceed $275,000 over two years, and no more than $200,000 in any single year
Specific Aims limited to 1 page; Research Strategy limited to 6 pages

structure.template: NIH R21 Research Plan: Specific Aims and Research Strategy

core_sections.name: Specific Aims
required: The gap or problem and why it matters now
Long-term goal, objective of this application and central hypothesis
Two to three specific aims, each with its expected outcome
Expected payoff: what the results enable next

core_sections.name: Significance
required: The important problem or critical barrier the project addresses
Rigor of the prior research the project builds on, and its weaknesses
How success would change scientific knowledge, technical capability or clinical practice

core_sections.name: Innovation
required: How the concepts, approaches or methods depart from current research paradigms
Refinement or new application of methods, stated concretely against named existing approaches

core_sections.name: Approach
required: Overall strategy, methodology and analyses for each aim
Data sources, cohort definition, outcome definition and evaluation design, including baselines
Strategies for scientific rigor and to guard against overfitting and site effects
Potential problems, alternative strategies and benchmarks for success
Timeline across the two-year project period

rules: Significance, Innovation and Approach together form the Research Strategy and must fit within 6 pages (roughly 3,000-3,300 words including figures)
Specific Aims is limited to 1 page
Investigators, Environment, budget, human subjects and data sharing sections are outside the scope of this document
